question: Should OpenClaw add a core startup-loaded immutable operator policy/defaults layer that enforces locked settings at runtime, or keep policy as conformance-only plus existing Nix/gateway guards?
rationale: The choice changes operator-vs-agent authority, config precedence, diagnostics, and which writes must fail closed, so automation should not pick the security contract.

options.title: Design core immutable policy
options.body: Add the feature as a core security boundary with explicit precedence, write rejection, doctor/status reporting, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep Policy conformance-only
options.body: Close or narrow this request after documenting that Policy reports drift while runtime enforcement remains limited to current Nix and gateway guards.

options.title: Defer to hook/API design
options.body: Wait for the related hook/provenance proposals if maintainers want plugin-owned policy engines rather than a core immutable overlay.

recommendation.title: Design core immutable policy
recommendation.body: Add the feature as a core security boundary with explicit precedence, write rejection, doctor/status reporting, and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the issue and authored the prior direct implementation attempt for the same boundary.
